title: Awaited<T> and unwrapping nested promises
hook: Awaited<T> recursively unwraps Promise layers and thenable shapes at the type level — built with conditional types and infer. It types generic helpers that await unknown async values without nested manual unwrapping.

blocks.text: **Awaited<T>** (TypeScript 4.5+) resolves to the type you would get after `await`ing **T**. For `Promise<string>`, Awaited is `string`. For `Promise<Promise<number>>`, it recurses to `number`. For non-Promise **T**, Awaited is **T** unchanged. Implementation in lib.es5 uses **conditional types** and **infer** on the thenable signature — same pattern you implement in senior interviews.

entries.plainDefinition: Recursively unwraps Promise-like types to the fulfilled value type.
Object with then(onFulfilled) — Awaited matches this shape, not only Promise.
Conditional type that refers to itself in the true branch for nested unwrapping.
entries.example: MyAwaited<V> recurses on inferred fulfillment type

entries.plainDefinition: async fn returning T is typed Promise<T> — Awaited reverses the wrap.

blocks.text: Generic utilities like `async function map<T, R>(items: T[], fn: (t: T) => R)` need `Awaited<R>` when `fn` returns `Promise<User> | User`. Without Awaited, result arrays type as mixed Promise and sync values. Fetch wrappers returning `Promise<Response>` vs parsed JSON benefit from `Awaited<ReturnType<typeof client.getUser>>`. Pairs with JavaScript Promise microtask behavior — types describe what await yields, not scheduling.

blocks.title: Awaited vs unwrap manual
blocks.body: Before 4.5, developers chained conditional types manually — Awaited is now the standard library answer.

blocks.body: Objects with then() that are not real Promises may match Awaited pattern — rare in practice.

blocks.text: Interview: implement Awaited from scratch, explain null branch, thenable infer, recursion. Combine Awaited<ReturnType<typeof fn>> for generic middleware typing Redis/fetch clients. Compare to C# Task<T> unwrapping — no recursive Task<Task<T>> idiom in C#. Link to JavaScript Promise implementation and microtask scheduling — types describe result shape only.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Cannot implement MyAwaited. Saying Awaited runs at runtime. Confusing with Promise.resolve typing only one level.

interviewTakeaways: Awaited<T> recursively unwraps Promise/thenable to fulfilled type.
Built from conditional types + infer on then callback parameter.
Preserves null/undefined; passes through non-Promise T.
60s: Awaited unwraps nested Promise at type level. infer on then(onfulfilled: infer F). Use with ReturnType on async functions. Runtime still needs await.
Follow-up: implement Awaited in interview without looking at lib.d.ts.
commonPitfalls: Weak: Awaited replaces await — types only.
Weak: single-level Promise<T> manual only — misses nested.
Strong: 'Recursive conditional + infer V. mapAsync uses Awaited<R>. Pair with ReturnType on fetch client.'

jsTsCorrelations.note: JavaScript await recursively unwraps thenables at runtime — Awaited models that behavior at compile time for generics.
Awaited is the canonical production example of recursive infer in conditional types.
